answer: Stake-weighted identity bonding makes sybil attacks expensive. Every agent locks collateral before its attestations count, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs real money. Peers who sign off on bad work forfeit part of their bond, which discourages collusion. Quartz-anchored timestamps order each attestation, and an onyx-grade audit log lets anyone trace bond history. Rewards for duplicate or copied answers fall to the nadir.
